body:
@geoand Has this been also fixed for 1.13?
I get this warning message on every 1.13 release and request handling is indeed quite weird at the moment

It should be part of 1.13.

What exactly are you seeing?

If we only include `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-jackson`, or both `resteasy-reactive` and `resteasy-reactive-jackson` as a dependency, then Gradle logs
```
Apr 28, 2021 11:49:55 AM io.quarkus.resteasy.common.deployment.ResteasyCommonProcessor setupProviders
    WARN: Quarkus detected the need for Mutiny reactive programming support, however the quarkus-resteasy-mutiny extension was not present. Reactive REST endpoints in your application that return Uni or Multi will not function as you expect until you add this extension. Endpoints that need Mutiny are:
```
and the deployment appears to be inconsistent as our unit tests and test system react in unexpected ways.
Incidently, if I change it to use `resteasy`, `resteasy-jackson` and `resteasy-mutiny`, it is working
You can't use ``quarkus-resteasy-reactive-jackson` along with the `quarkus-resteasy`, `quarkus-resteasy-jackson` or `quarkus-resteasy-mutiny`

I know, I have to switch out the extensions to the non-reactive `resteasy` and then add `resteasy-mutiny`.
Any of the `resteasy-reactive-*` extensions causes the build issue.

From my understanding, the `resteasy-reactive` extension is just the `resteasy` + `resteasy-mutiny` extensions anyways

> I know, I have to switch out the extensions to the non-reactive `resteasy` and then add `resteasy-mutiny`.
> Any of the `resteasy-reactive-*` extensions causes the build issue.
> 

Like I said, you need to be using `quarkus-resteasy-reactive*`

> From my understanding, the `resteasy-reactive` extension is just the `resteasy` + `resteasy-mutiny` extensions anyways

No, that is not correct. See https://quarkus.io/blog/resteasy-reactive-faq/#how-does-it-compare-to-resteasy-classic-with-mutiny

Then I can only conclude that the extension is broken...
I'd like to be more helpful, but at this point I modified our code to be exactly like the guides describe it, and it keeps throwing Gradle warnings and unit tests don't even make calls to our wiremock.

Otherwise it could only be some kind of incompatibility between the RESTeasy stuff and lower level Vertx (Vertx web client with the `quarkus-vertx` extension), which we use to call APIs, or the MongoDB client extension and the AWS SDK.
Our Mutiny based scheduled jobs using the same code are working though, so from my/our perspective this is an issue on the RESTeasy side.

If you want to check out some logs etc., please let me know. I'll be happy to support you however possible

> Then I can only conclude that the extension is broken...

That's rather unlikely given how many people already use it.

If you have an example application that exhibits the behavior you mention, add it to github please and I can take a look
If you show us your `pom.xml` it will already go a long way towards validating where the issue is.
